extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of public administration, policymakers, and government reformers
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing and evaluating the design and reform of government administrative systems, especially the tradeoffs between centralization, civil service reform, and political party organization. Emphasis on how structure affects administrative efficiency, patronage, and popular government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of competitive examinations for lower-level positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive examinations can, in the nature of things, be applied successfully only to comparatively unimportant positions in the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examinations justify adoption if they relieve lower branches of the service from the influence of politics and impress on the public that political parties need not control officers whose duty is to aid execution of the laws. They are chiefly for subordinate/clerical/subordinate forces, not necessarily for high offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and retention of important officers based on fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers such as chiefs of divisions, collectors of customs and internal revenue, postmasters, even, in many cases, commissioners of bureaus, shall be selected on account of fitness for their positions, and shall, so long as they give evidence of such fitness, be retained in office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote appointment based on demonstrated competence and retention contingent on continued evidence of fitness; this is an argument for merit-based selection extending beyond only low-level positions as public opinion demands it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralize administration to suit changed social and technological conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative system had to be centralized to suit changed conditions (growth of urban life, steam and electricity, railroads, telegraph, telephone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When population density and interconnectedness increase administrative tasks and unite previously separated functions, centralization is necessary for efficiency. Historical example: shift from stage-coach/mail-carrier era to railroad/telegraph era.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralize municipal administration under a strong mayor where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been an almost universal movement toward according the mayor the same position in the city that the President has come to occupy in the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrating municipal administration under the mayor increases capacity to handle complex urban problems; legal changes may be required because municipal traditions/statutes differ from national evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-level central administrative supervision for complex functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The tendency in most of the states whose civilization is most complex is toward administrative centralization and away from their original unconcentrated administrative conditions (e.g., supervision of banking, insurance, transportation, inspection of factories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create state central administrations (State Boards of Equalization, State Superintendents of Schools, Boards of Charities and Prisons) to exercise supervision over functions that local bodies previously managed inadequately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompany centralization with recognition of a sphere where politics are minimized
rubrics_metrics.description: This centralization should be accompanied by a fuller recognition of a sphere of government where the influence of politics is baneful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not centralize alone; safeguard certain administrative functions from partisan influence to preserve administrative efficiency and popular government. Centralization without such recognition invites party misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect administration by granting reasonably permanent tenure and demanding impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralization of administration without the recognition of the necessity for officers who, like judges, should have a reasonably permanent tenure and of whom impartiality in their actions may be demanded, tends to increase the influence of party leaders at the expense of the power of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement tenure and impartiality safeguards for administrative officers to prevent centralization from becoming an instrument of party leaders that can thwart the popular will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate expression and execution of state will via governmental structure or parties
rubrics_metrics.description: If this coordination of the expression and the execution of the will of the state is not brought about in the governmental system, it must be provided for outside of the government; where found outside, it is to be found in the political party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure effective mechanisms (either internal governmental centralization and legislative control or organized party structures) so that laws expressed by the state are actually executed in harmony with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match party organization strength to the degree of governmental centralization/concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Party organization is based on the character and amount of the work the party has to do; the work the party has to do depends very largely on the relations existing both between different organs of the central government and between the central and the local governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where government is decentralized and unconcentrated, parties must be stronger, more complicated, and more permanent to secure harmony between lawmaking and execution; where government is centralized, parties can differ in necessary strength but still usually must be reasonably strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive partisan control and patronage in centralized administrations
rubrics_metrics.description: A centralized administrative system, in which the influence of politics is strong, can easily be made use of to further the interests of the political party at the expense of ease in the expression of the popular will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize danger of centralized administration being exploited by irresponsible party leaders for patronage; curb partisan distribution of favors that impairs administrative efficiency and thwarts expressed public will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil service reform often depends on prior centralization
rubrics_metrics.description: The movement to separate Administration from politics did not begin until the old American system of administration had been abandoned and our faces had been turned in the direction of administrative centralization. The first law providing for examinations ... was passed about the time it was recognized that the national administrative system was centralized under the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: reforms like competitive examinations and permanent municipal services are more feasible and effective once administrative structure is centralized sufficiently to make merit systems workable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize tradeoffs of party weakness vs. party strength in different constitutional systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the executive is largely independent of the legislature, weak parties are accompanied by methods of government which may not be called popular. Where the executive is dependent on the legislature, weak parties are too apt to be accompanied by inefficient administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess constitutional context: in executive-independent systems, parties must be strong to ensure popular control; in parliamentary/dependent-executive systems, parties must be strong to secure efficient administration. Weak parties can produce either unresponsive government or administrative inefficiency depending on system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor national party organization to reduce local patron-client excesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidates of strong national parties owe allegiance primarily to the party, and only secondarily to their immediate constituents; local parties are often based on grossly material motives and personal patronage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong national parties help align representatives with party platforms and national principles rather than personal favors; local/personal-based parties encourage patronage and misuse of governmental power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware that strong parties can become self-perpetuating machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Strongly organized national parties are made use of by designing persons for corrupt and selfish ends and sometimes become mere machines whose main purpose is self-perpetuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While strong parties are generally preferable to local patronage, implement checks because party machines can subvert ideals; promote principles-based party allegiance rather than pure self-interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization plus fragmented/localized party systems undermines administrative efficiency (France/Italy example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The French and Italian cases show centralized administration paired with weak or local party systems leads ministers to distribute favors to secure votes, impairing administrative efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the institutional combination where a highly centralized administration is controlled by fragmented/local patronage-driven parties; such combinations incentivize stopping services or misallocating resources to secure local votes (e.g., trains stopping at many stations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent parties from performing functions better placed within government
rubrics_metrics.description: Where provision is not made for coordination in the governmental system, it must be made outside of it, and this can be done only through the party — only through recognizing the propriety of insisting on political tests for officers charged with executing the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design government institutions to assume coordination roles where appropriate rather than relying excessively on parties to fill structural gaps; reliance on parties for core administrative coordination risks patronage and instability.
